data.claim: The docs (D-DRV-6 + driver-architecture research) promise ddflow model show|lint|probe|resolve, but the shipped parser registers only show.
data.falsifier: grep of the two driver-architecture docs for "model show|lint|probe|resolve" returns >=1 match while the parser registers no lint/probe/resolve.
data.mechanism: parsers/workflow.py registers model subcommand show only; model_cmds.py has model_show only.
data.probe_output: matched D-DRV-6 row and research bullet; ddflow model --help showed usage: ddflow model {show} only
data.question: Does ddflow model ship only show, while docs promise show|lint|probe|resolve?

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only rejects the single substring `model show|lint|probe|resolve`. A doc (or the DRV-cli task title this change never edits) that says `ddflow model lint`, `ddflow model probe`, and `ddflow model resolve` as separate verbs does not contain that substring, so `test_driver_docs_do_not_over_promise_model_cli_verbs` passes while the bug’s promise is still there. The same check never opens the task record the bug names as the other source of the promise.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_model_cli_doc_parity.py:17

chunk_findings.detail: D-DRV-6 is still labeled DECIDED after an in-place cut from `model show|lint|probe|resolve` to `model show` only, with no override note of the kind D-DRV-8 uses in the same table. A reader of the decision file is told that “show only” is what was decided, which is false: this diff is what deleted the other verbs, and they are still unimplemented. The research bullet now also assigns resolve’s job to `show` (“prints each fact with source and date”) without any check that `ddflow model show` does that.

chunk_findings.detail: The edited D-DRV-6 cell is still status DECIDED and now states the CLI as `` `ddflow model show|lint|probe|resolve` ``, the exact unimplemented promise bug B57b8dcef42 asked to implement or remove. The parenthetical “shipped: `ddflow model show` only” does not override that contract the way D-DRV-8’s override note does, so a reader (or a search for the bug’s signature string) still treats lint, probe, and resolve as the decided model surface. `test_decision_drv6_notes_the_shipped_model_surface` never rejects those verbs; it only requires the shipped note somewhere in the file, so the regression passes while the promise is present. `test_research_doc_does_not_promise_model_cli_verbs_beyond_show` does not read this decision file at all.

A reader (or `ddflow model lint`) still gets the promise B57b8dcef42 is about; the parenthetical does not delete it and is not an override of the D-DRV-8 kind. The new regression locks that in: `_STALE_CLI` names that exact string as a stale over-promise, but only `test_research_doc_does_not_promise_model_cli_verbs_beyond_show` searches for it. `test_decision_drv6_notes_the_shipped_model_surface` never checks `rows` for those verbs — it only requires "`ddflow model show` only" and "read-only" somewhere in the file — so this decision text passes while the bug’s promise is in the file this diff edits.

Given research text `ddflow model show\|lint\|probe\|resolve` (the escaped-pipe form the old assertion was written to catch), `"ddflow model show|lint|probe|resolve" not in text` is true, so `test_research_doc_does_not_promise_model_cli_verbs_beyond_show` passes while the verbs are still named.
